deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematical derivations. It is a draft of the opening of §3 ('Stetigkeit der geraden Linie' / transition to §4) of Dedekind's 'Stetigkeit und irrationale Zahlen' (1872). It continues the previous page's demand that arithmetic develop 'aus sich selbst heraus'. The argument runs as follows.

(1) Dedekind concedes that links to non-arithmetical ideas, such as extensive magnitudes and measurement, were historically the immediate occasion for extending the number concept. He adds the parenthetical exception 'not for the complex numbers'.

(2) He holds that this historical fact is no reason to bring such foreign considerations into arithmetic, the science of numbers, itself.

(3) He gives an analogy, in modern terms. Z is built from N, and Q is built from Z, by a 'free (pure) creation'. The arithmetic laws on Z and Q are reduced to those on N. He underlines 'sollte': 'so it at least should be done', a remark on the state of rigour at the time. In the same way, the irrationals must be defined purely in terms of Q. 'Only the How? remains the question.'

(4) The earlier comparison of Q with a straight line showed Q to be gappy ('lückenhaft', incomplete, discontinuous). We ascribe completeness, i.e. continuity, to the line. The question 'what does this continuity consist in?' must contain everything; the next page adds that only through it is a scientific foundation for all continuous domains obtained.

(5) A marginal note reads 'Vage Reden über den Zusammenhang in den kleinsten Theilen'. It is the seed of the published sentence 'Mit vagen Reden über den ununterbrochenen Zusammenhang in den kleinsten Teilen ist natürlich nichts erreicht'.

The next page then states the answer: the cut principle for the line. If the points of the line split into two classes A1, A2 with every point of A1 left of every point of A2, there is exactly one point producing the cut. In modern terms this is order-completeness (Dedekind completeness) of a linear order.

The text corresponds closely, often verbatim, to the printed 1872 text. The printed version has these differences:
- 'mag im allgemeinen zugegeben werden' for 'ist nicht zu leugnen'.
- A strengthened complex-number parenthesis.
- 'zurückgeführt werden müssen und können' replacing the bracket '(so sollte es wenigstens geschehen)'.
- 'durch die rationalen Zahlen allein vollständig definiert werden'.
- The symbol R for the rational domain.
- 'Lückenlosigkeit' added.
- The marginal note worked into the main text.
errors: No mathematical errors; the page contains no computation.

Historically, the parenthetical claim that complex numbers were not introduced via non-arithmetical (geometric) considerations is debatable. Complex numbers arose algebraically (Cardano, Bombelli), but their acceptance owed much to geometric representation (Wessel, Argand, Gauss). Dedekind's claim concerns the origin, which is defensible.

results.what: Programmatic demand that irrational numbers be defined purely from the rationals, by analogy with the construction of negative and fractional numbers from the natural numbers, excluding geometric/measurement notions from arithmetic.
results.modern_name: Arithmetization of analysis; constructive definition of R from Q
results.usually_credited_to: Dedekind (1872), contemporaneously Cantor, Heine, Méray, Weierstrass

results.what: Posing the question 'what does the continuity of the line consist in?' as the key to founding all continuous domains, rejecting vague talk of 'connection in the smallest parts'.
results.modern_name: Dedekind completeness / continuity axiom (answered on next page by the cut principle)
results.usually_credited_to: Dedekind, Stetigkeit und irrationale Zahlen (1872; idea dated 24 Nov 1858)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of the well-known published text of 'Stetigkeit und irrationale Zahlen' §3, nearly verbatim. The only points of interest are minor drafting variants: the underlined 'sollte' remark about rigour for Q, the inserted 'reine' Schöpfung, and the marginal note that became a published sentence.

checkable.asserts: sqrt(2) is irrational, i.e. Q has gaps relative to the line (the background claim of 'Lückenhaftigkeit').

checkable.sympy: all((sympy.Rational(p,q)**2 != 2) for p in range(1,200) for q in range(1,200))
checkable.asserts: No rational p/q (sampled) squares to 2, so the cut {x: x<=0 or x**2<2} | {x: x>0, x**2>2} of Q has no rational boundary point.
